Doctor is one planned entry/orchestration workflow with separate modules for data/Free-R/refinement diagnostics, CIF/effective-restraint assessment, and model geometry/connectivity assessment with guided sticky-end repair. Prefer an audited ReadySet wrapper and a mandatory effective-result audit before POSTMR_READY over replacing ReadySet chemistry generation wholesale. Early source screening helps failures before ReadySet; the post-ReadySet native interpretation is authoritative.

Keep graph identity, numerical parameterization, effective native interpretation, achieved geometry, diffraction fit and intended assembly as separate evidence dimensions. None substitutes for the others.

A fixer may automate an exact reviewed, hash/version-scoped transformation. Otherwise assess, propose and retain ambiguity; do not invent tautomer, protonation, bond order, pucker, distance, coordination or strand connections.
Do not reproduce chemistry defects by deriving replacement targets from the distorted model being evaluated. Preserve source descriptors and use independently qualified generator/reference evidence.

SMILES is optional graph evidence with explicit provenance, not a CIF numerical validator and not automatic chemical truth. Source descriptors can disagree with the selected explicit graph, as DP phosphate charges demonstrate.
Never regenerate or search alternative Free-R flags to improve statistics. Keep observations and test-set authority fixed across dictionary/coordinate trials.

After MR/refinement, inspect geometry/connectivity before spending additional strategy trials on an identified structural defect, even if numerical readiness has passed. Route declared arm defects through guided preview and bounded checkpoint repair.
The GeoTest campaign is wrapped for orchestration. Its provisional structures are future test fixtures, not additional work required to close that scope.
